exposure: epidural/spinal anesthesia use during vaginal birth
cohort: 106 women who gave birth within twelve months prior to completing the survey
finding: PPP was prevalent in this sample, and while the intensity of pain was on average, mild, the pain was widespread in terms of location and triggers, with multiple biopsychosocial factors differentiating women with persistent postpartum pain from those women whose pain resolved.
mod_finding: Women with PPP were more likely to have had a Caesarean section (15.2% versus 33.3%) compared to women whose acute pain resolved after childbirth.
